text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran the active/active handoff e2e with tenant-residency=STRICT, triggered failover eu->us-west, hit weird tombstone behavior on writes

sam: can you summarise what failed?

maria: short: standby promoted but some tenants stayed 'tombstoned' in kv-owner table, writes got 409 / tombstone until we cleared entries manually

dinesh: ugh. repro script or steps?

maria: steps: create tenant T123 (residency=eu), attach session, write a few docs, simulate eu-primary crash, promote standby, run client traffic against us-west. Observe 409s for new writes.

kevin: do we still have TTL-based tombstones? or explicit quarantine markers?

maria: quarantine marker; we mark tenant as quarantined during eviction window, then write path checks: if quarantine==true -> respond tombstone

casey: are we clearing quarantine on successful takeover? that sounds like the missing step

dinesh: logs from runtime: 
```
I0321 12:03:11 runtime.go:412] tenant=T123 state=quarantined lease_owner=eu-primary
I0321 12:03:24 runtime.go:487] lease-swap attempt: new_owner=us-west result=promoted
I0321 12:03:31 runtime.go:498] write-reject: tenant=T123 reason=tombstone_quarantine remain=true
```

sam: thanks. so promote succeeded but the quarantine flag lived in an external kv (ownership table) and wasn't updated by the promote path?

dinesh: looks like promote flow only flips lease_owner but leaves quarantine bit-set; we intentionally separate them to avoid race during eviction, but we didn't implement a gc/handshake to clear quarantine after a successful takeover

maria: exact. result: clients hit write guard that checks quarantine before allowing writer to bypass prefix-caching.

kevin: two immediate options: 1) make promote atomic and clear quarantine in the same transaction as lease_owner flip (hard cross-region txn), 2) add a post-promote handshake where new owner does a verification read and clears quarantine if safe

casey: +3 add a short lived 'pending' state instead of boolean quarantine. pending->promoted->cleared gives more visibility

dinesh: agree. tradeoffs: atomic cross-region txn is ideal w.r.t correctness but adds latency and is operationally scary; handshake adds complexity but is async and simpler to implement

sam: also think about consent/data residency: we can't clear quarantine automatically if the promoted region is not consented by that tenant. That must remain enforced

maria: good catch — in test tenant had eu consent only, but we were promoting to us-west because forced failover; policy says promote allowed for disaster but quarantine clearing needs explicit policy check

kevin: so flow should be: promote -> new_owner evaluates residency policy -> if allowed then run handshake to clear quarantine and resume writes -> if not allowed keep tombstone and route reads-only or show error to client + ops alert

casey: for handshake, propose a bounded retry with idempotent ops: new_owner writes "clear-intent" record, waits for ack from quorum (or durable write), then flips local cache and emits event. We can rely on our durable replication within region — no cross-region txn required

maria: rough sequence I sketched: 
1) promote sets lease_owner=us-west, sets takeover_timestamp
2) new owner checks residency policy; if allowed, new owner writes clear-intent -> durable local write
3) a background reconciler consumes clear-intent and clears quarantine flag in kv-owner table
4) reconciler emits event that allows write path to accept writes

sam: does step 3 require a global update? the kv-owner table is the source of truth for quarantine bit
dinesh: kv-owner is multi-region replicated via async pipeline; reconciler writing locally will replicate. there will be a window where some replicas still see quarantine, but new owner can serve because it has seen clear-intent and local cleared flag. clients routed to other regions may keep seeing 409 until replication finishes — acceptable with warning

kevin: need to update client routing: during takeover window we should prefer routing to new_owner until replication finishes; otherwise application gets inconsistent errors

casey: add short TTL-based override for clients with escalation token so SEs can continue writes for troubleshooting

maria: good. I also hit an edge: if promote fails midway we might leave clear-intent without owner — reconciler must garbage collect stale clear-intents older than X and reapply quarantine if owner not stable

sam: operational: expose metrics: number of tombstones, quarantines cleared, pending clear-intents, last-promote-duration
dinesh: I'll draft a small RFC follow-up proposing handshake + reconciler + policy check + GC. Will include sequence diagram and failure modes.

maria: thanks. please include test matrix: consented vs non-consented, fast failover vs manual promote, proxy routing scenarios
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: e2e-handshake-test-suite -> started (build #432) :rocket:

sam: once RFC up we'll schedule a short arch sync to approve. prefer lightweight change first (handshake) then consider atomic txn long-term

maria: agreed. thanks all :thumbsup:
